documentation.range: Muraena helena is known from the eastern Atlantic from the south of the British Isles to Senegal, including the Mediterranean, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands and Cape Verde. It has a depth range of 15-50 m.
documentation.population: Muraena helena is common in parts of its range.
documentation.habitats: Muraena helena is associated with rocky bottoms, and is commonly found in holes, and crevices amongst rock at depths of 15-50 m. It is a nocturnal and territorial species (Gothel 1992). This species feeds on fish, crabs and squid (Gothel 1992).
documentation.threats: Despite the minor usage of this species, it is not considered to have any major threats.
documentation.measures: There are no species-specific conservation measures in place for this species. It has a distribution that overlaps with marine reserves in parts of its range.
documentation.use_trade: This species is of a minor  commercial importance as food and is sometimes taken for public display  aquariums. It is utilized fresh and eaten broiled, boiled and baked. The skin  can be used for leather (Frimody 1995).
documentation.rationale: Muraena helena is widely distributed in the eastern Atlantic, and is common in parts of its range. It is harvested for food and is a minor component of the aquarium trade. There are no indications at present time of population declines from harvesting. It is therefore listed as Least Concern, with a recommendation for continued monitoring of its population status.
